items.desc: During a private visit to Bethanchok, Prince Louis pledged continued support for education and environmental conservation and met local representatives to discuss post-disaster recovery.

items.desc: The former RSP joint general secretary has yet to say whether she will contest as an independent or represent another political party.

items.title: Nepal urges China to reopen Tatopani border crossing
items.desc: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal tells a visiting Chinese delegation that the crossing is crucial to connectivity, as the Rasuwagadhi route remains shut following the August floods.

items.title: Xi, Putin blast Western ‘protectionism’, sanctions before meeting Trump at APEC
items.desc: The remarks came ahead of a high-stakes trilateral meeting with Donald Trump, where the three leaders are expected to discuss the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade and other global flashpoints.

items.title: Police inspector found dead at official residence in Gulmi
items.desc: The 52-year-old officer was found unresponsive in his bed after colleagues broke open a window when he failed to wake up.

items.title: Second Mahadevtar tunnel bore breaks through Kathmandu-Tarai Expressway
items.desc: The 3.445-km tunnel is one of two parallel bores at Mahadevtar. The Kathmandu-Tarai Expressway remains only about 50 percent complete after nine years of construction.

items.title: Kathmandu Valley begins selling meat with safety stamps
items.desc: The government has deployed 240 trained inspectors to enforce meat inspection rules, with plans to make certification compulsory across the country by July 2027.

items.title: Kathmandu is going digital. Its birds and animals are paying the price
items.desc: Telecom towers, data centres, floodlights and tangled fibre networks are disrupting the habitats and natural cycle of birds and animals. Yet the ecological consequences of this expanding infrastructure remain largely unstudied.

items.title: Five takeaways from Trump’s Asia tour: cabinet feuds, Rubio love and a Kim Jong Un curveball
items.desc: As Trump prepares for high-stakes talks in China, problems at home and divisions within his administration have followed him on his Asian tour.

items.title: How India became a rice powerhouse and why it’s becoming a problem
items.desc: Advances in crop science and decades of subsidies have driven Indian rice production to record levels, but mounting surpluses are straining public finances, storage capacity and relations with competing exporters.

items.title: Kathmandu Gorkhas and Chitwan Rhinos target first Eliminator win
items.desc: Having suffered exits in their previous playoff appearances, both franchises collide in a do-or-die battle to advance to Qualifier 2.

items.title: Defending champion Lumbini Lions cruise into the final
items.desc: The Lions defeated Sudurpaschim Royals by 6 wickets in Qualifier 1 on Tuesday. Sudurpaschim, meanwhile, still have a chance to reach the final by winning Qualifier 2.

items.title: Why has Election Commission yet to update Nepali Congress leadership records?
items.desc: The commission says it is still examining documents and constitutional amendments submitted by the party, but the delay has raised questions within the Congress amid a lingering dispute over its leadership.

items.title: Flood victims occupy Nepal Electricity Authority land, erect tents
items.desc: More than 250 displaced families from Trishuli Bazar cleared the land using an excavator, accusing the government of delaying their rehabilitation.

items.title: At Nepal tax awards, finance minister raises low investment paradox
items.desc: As the government honours top taxpayers for their fiscal contributions, businesses caution that structural bottlenecks, policy instability, and market risks continue to dampen long-term investment appetite.

items.title: Millions flowed into former teacher Inam Sapkota’s account in a year
items.desc: Bank records show Rs63.1 million deposited into the fixer’s account, with large sums transferred to company accounts soon afterwards.

items.title: Shah must use his India visit to push for progress on longstanding issues
items.desc: The prime minister must firmly advance Nepal’s interests while deepening bilateral cooperation.

items.title: What Mithila’s stray bulls tell us about Nepal’s economy
items.desc: An economy built on exporting its youth and taxing its imports is not developing; it is liquidating its future.

items.title: How crony capitalism keeps Nepalis poor
items.desc: Since 1990, favouring connections over competence may have kept Nepali incomes a third below their potential.

items.title: Nepali youth press COP31 presidency for grants to rebuild after disasters
items.desc: Activists tell Australian negotiators in Antalya that countries that did little to cause the climate crisis should not have to borrow to recover from it.

items.title: Last-minute push to secure mountain agenda in COP31 outcome
items.desc: The latest draft proposes a dedicated programme on mountain regions, but Nepal wants clear commitments on climate adaptation, research and finance.

items.title: Explained: Nepal and India have revived stalled air route talks. Here’s what you need to know
items.desc: Kathmandu is pushing for two-way access to the Mahendranagar route, stalled by security concerns and strategic mistrust for years.

items.title: Dipendra’s half-century fails to lift Sudurpaschim as Lumbini restrict them to 105
items.desc: Sudurpaschim managed just 20 runs in the opening powerplay before their captain scored a fighting 52, but the Royals were bowled out of momentum and finished on 105 for eight in Qualifier 1.

items.title: ‘Death is near’: Inside the hoax bomb threats that rattled Europe’s schools and airports
items.desc: Most targets were schools in the ​United Kingdom, Ireland and Italy. But media organisations, airlines, airports, charities and private individuals were also caught up in the campaign.

items.title: Lumbini Lions and Sudurpaschim Royals eye final spot
items.desc: The winners of Qualifier 1 will advance directly to the Nepal Premier League final, while the losing side will get another chance through Qualifier 2.

items.title: Dhiraaj Rajbanshi on filming ‘Himalayan Gold’, a yarsagumba thriller, above 3,800 metres
items.desc: The director's debut film, out on Friday, explores a little-seen world of Nepal’s mountain communities. He says the story began with tales of robberies in Rukum highlands.

items.title: How individual labour permits for Europe grew 22-fold in five years
items.desc: A new study says the suspension of demand-letter verification has pushed job seekers to informal agents, exposing them to fraud, debt and exploitation.

items.title: Police seize Rs16.7 million in unaccounted cash in Lalitpur
items.desc: A team from the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office recovered the money after receiving information about a suspicious financial transaction.
